title: trail_ring_stationary_no_push pins a stationary echo push while its comment asserts the opposite; the real no-push invariant is never exercised
detail: The first call is a snap (early return, no push), so trail_n==1 can only come from the stationary second call: the test pins a stationary push while asserting the opposite. The non-empty-ring stationary case is never exercised.
recommended_fix: Seed the ring with a genuinely moving frame first, then assert the stationary frame leaves trail_n unchanged; or make the empty-ring push require actual movement and update the expectation.

title: PR body claims snapshot mode reproduces the pre-2.1 render "byte-identically", but the code applies the +15% packet size in both modes
detail: The BEFORE strips carry the +15% packet radius, so they are not byte-identical pre-2.1 renders. The evidence-pack claim overstates what the tool produces; N9 corrected the code comment but not the PR body.
recommended_fix: Reword the PR body to "snapshot-exact positions (the +15% size applies in both modes — only the glide differs)", matching the render_strip_frame comment.

title: Both CI files invoke `tools/harness.sh motion-pixel`, but this diff contains no change to tools/harness.sh
evidence:
ci.yml: "- name: Motion-readability activation (rlsw pixel midpoint)
        run: tools/harness.sh motion-pixel" — ci-local.sh: "  \"Motion-readability activation (rlsw pixel: the alpha=0.5 glide midpoint)|tools/harness.sh motion-pixel\"" — no hunk for tools/harness.sh exists anywhere in this diff.
detail: If harness.sh enumerates verbs (a dispatcher) rather than forwarding "$@", the new gate fails or silently no-ops. Notably the README invokes motion-strip via ./bin/harness directly, not via harness.sh.
recommended_fix: Verify/add the motion-pixel case in tools/harness.sh, or invoke ./bin/harness motion-pixel directly in CI exactly as the README does for motion-strip.

title: motion_pixel_setup indexes flow.packets[0] before the graceful length check runs
evidence:
setup: "pp.flow_try_spawn(state, cat, 0, a, c, 4) // the packet's spawn_tick is 4
	pk := &state.flow.packets[0]" — guard only later, in the caller: "motion_pixel_setup(&state, cat)
	if len(state.flow.packets) != 1 {
		fmt.eprintfln(\"motion-pixel: expected 1 packet, got %d\", len(state.flow.packets))
		return 2""
detail: If flow_try_spawn produces no packet, the unchecked packets[0] dereference panics before the intended exit-2 diagnostics can fire — the guard is dead in exactly the case it was written for.
recommended_fix: Check len(state.flow.packets) >= 1 inside motion_pixel_setup before taking the pointer (return an error string), or move the spawn into run_motion_pixel after the guard.

title: Docs and CI comment claim "13" motion tests; motion_test.odin contains 18 @(test) procs
evidence:
README: "`app/render/motion_test.odin` (13 new `@(test)`s, in the gate-2 render test run)" — ci.yml: "# motion-readability pins live here: motion_test.odin's 13 interp
# pins + trails_active + the activation derivation" — yet the file also declares "@(test)
activation_running_clamps_accum_fraction", "@(test)
activation_not_running_snapshot_exact", "@(test)
trail_ring_order_and_fill", "@(test)
trail_ring_stationary_no_push", "@(test)
trail_fades_newest_strongest" (5 beyond the r1-era 13).
detail: The r3 additions (activation + trail-ring sections f and g) were appended without updating the r1-era counts in the README and the CI comment; the coverage claim understates the suite.
recommended_fix: Update README and the ci.yml comment to 18 tests (or "13 interp pins + 5 r3 activation/ring pins").

title: Redundant `_ = bw` discard in motion_pixel_setup after bw is already used
evidence:
"bw := u32(cat.balance.packet_bandwidth)
	pp.flow_try_spawn(state, cat, 0, a, c, 4) // the packet's spawn_tick is 4
	pk := &state.flow.packets[0]
	...
	pk.progress_units = (bw * 3) / 8 // frac 0.375 at tick 4
	_ = bw"
detail: bw is consumed by the progress_units assignment; the trailing `_ = bw` is a dead leftover (probably from an edit that moved the usage) and only adds noise.

title: motion_pixel.odin ships a verbatim-duplicated NEGATIVE CONTROL comment block and leftover "hmm, no:" reasoning scratch
detail: Copy-paste duplication and thinking-aloud text left in a shipped evidence-gate file undermine the carefully-polished tone the rest of the diff maintains and will confuse future maintainers.
recommended_fix: Delete the duplicate NEGATIVE CONTROL block and rewrite the "hmm, no" passage as a definitive statement.

title: Band comment says "scan y 190..300" but the code scans y 225..255
evidence:
Comment: "// along world y=10 (screen y ≈ 240 at the fit camera) — scan y 190..300
	// isolates the packet from the HUD (top ~150px) + buildings." — actual call: "cx, cy, ok := motion_pixel_centroid(img, 430, 610, 225, 255)"
detail: The stated scan band (190..300) does not match the executed band (225..255). A future maintainer widening the band per the comment could reintroduce the HUD/building pollution the tight band avoids.
recommended_fix: Update the comment to "scan y 225..255" (and x 430..610) to match the call.

title: motion_strip.odin header contains an orphaned sentence fragment from an earlier edit
detail: The line "the golden path (the harness's draw_world default) — so the same verb..." dangles after the rewritten parenthetical; it references wording that no longer precedes it, indicating a botched comment edit.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the bullet as one coherent sentence: "`snapshot` forces alpha=1.0 (the golden path's draw default), so the same verb produces both strips from the SAME sim timeline."

title: interp_continuous's doc comment is attached to interp_alpha_from_accum; interp_continuous is declared bare
detail: The interp_continuous description merges into interp_alpha_from_accum's doc block (comments attach to the next declaration), so generated docs/IDE hover attribute the continuity-guard docs to the wrong proc.
recommended_fix: Insert a blank line between the two comment blocks so each proc carries its own doc.
